newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Daewoo buys Moroccan hotel for $28.7 mln.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo buys Moroccan hotel for $28.7 mln.

text.p: South Korea's Daewoo corporation 8700.KS has bought Morocco's five-star Hyatt Regency hotel for $28.7 million and would invest up to $53 million in a two-year period, a Moroccan minister said on Friday.

"Daewoo Corporation agreed to pay $28.7 million for the purchase of the Hyatt Regency and up to $53 million for its renovation and extension in a two-year period starting from December 20, 1996, now," Trade Minister Driss Jettou told Reuters by telephone.
Built on eight-hectare (20 acre) site, the Hyatt Regency is located in a residential area, close to Rabat Royal palace.
The deal was signed late on Thursday night.
"We insisted that the hotel be managed by professionals. Therefore the hotel will be managed by the U.S. Hilton company," Jettou said.
That implies the hotel would change its title to Hilton Hotel as it was before 1988, he said.

Daewoo was continuing talks with the Moroccan authorities to implement an investment of $500 million in projects in the North African country covering telecommunications, tourism, electronics and the car industry.
"We expect the global deal to be sealed by March 1997...And the total amount of investments will increase substantially from the initial $500 million," Jettou said.
Daewoo signed an agreement of principle on the $500 million investment with the government last July in Rabat.

Jettou described the talks between Daewoo and state-owned Caisse de Depot et Gestion officials on the hotel sale as "very tough but a great step towards future partnership with South Korean investors."

"The move aimed at attracting a professional international investor and develop high standards of tourism accommodation from which the country will benefit in the long term," a Moroccan official said.
The Hyatt Regency has 220 rooms, 28 suites and employs a staff of more 300.
